question: Do wrist-worn accelerometer-measured physical activity and sleep patterns in daily life predict later disease and death? Need a few thousand adults, 1 week or more of wear, linked hospital/diagnosis/death outcomes, US university access by application.

requirements.text: Wrist-worn accelerometer/tracker worn in daily life for several days to a week or more
At least a few thousand adults
Linked follow-up outcomes: hospital records, diagnoses or death registration
Obtainable by a US university via application
Raw or near-raw signal, for comparability with other wrist studies

verification.found_title: Data Access Tiers – All of Us Research Hub

sentences: The Registered Tier dataset contains individual-level data, available only to registered researchers on the Researcher Workbench.
There are three tiers of data access: Public (no login required); Registered (login required); and Controlled (additional approval required).
Authorization for access to the registered and controlled data tiers will be user based, rather than project based.

Authorized users will receive a “data passport.” The data passport is required for gaining access to the registered and controlled data tiers and for creating workspaces to carry out research projects.

record.title: Minute level step counts and physical activity data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011-2014
record.description: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) is a nationally representative study that collects demographic, socioeconomic, dietary, and health-related information from 10,000 Americans annually. In Wave G (2011-2012) and Wave H (2013-2014), participants wore an ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven consecutive days. Publicly available data include minute-level wear predictions (wake wear, sleep wear, unknown, nonwear), data quality flags, and monitor-independent movement summary units (MIMS).
